holidays.name: National Cream-Filled Donut Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate fluffy fried dough stuffed with custard, cream, or whipped goodness. Sprinkles are optional, but napkins are not.
holidays.origin: Like many American food holidays, it was popularized by food-industry promoters and fans of donuts rather than established by an official government proclamation. It sits among a crowded calendar of donut days.
holidays.funFact: Donuts with filling are often called Berliner-style, and the filled version is said to have roots in German and Central European fried pastries that immigrants brought to America.

holidays.name: Eat a Hoagie Day
holidays.description: A salute to the mighty sub sandwich, especially the Philadelphia-area hoagie loaded with Italian meats, cheese, lettuce, onions, and oil and vinegar.
holidays.origin: The hoagie is tied to Philadelphia, where one popular origin story links the name to Italian workers at Hog Island shipyard during World War I, whose sandwiches became known as 'hoggies.' The day itself is an informal food observance.
holidays.funFact: In 1992, Philadelphia's Hoagie became a topic of civic pride so intense that locals still argue vigorously over whether a hoagie is properly a hoagie without sharp provolone.

holidays.name: Free Cone Day Season Kickoff: National Coloring Day
holidays.description: A day for grown-ups and kids alike to grab crayons, markers, and colored pencils and give themselves permission to color outside the lines. It is promoted as a stress-relieving creative break.
holidays.origin: National Coloring Day was popularized online by coloring-book brands and creative communities as the adult coloring trend took off in the 2010s. It is an unofficial observance with no formal founding authority.
holidays.funFact: The adult coloring book boom of the mid-2010s saw coloring books top bestseller lists, and some therapists noted that coloring can promote mindfulness.

holidays.name: Positive Thinking Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to flipping your inner grump into a glass-half-full thinker. Expect optimism, affirmations, and a ban on doom-scrolling, at least until lunch.
holidays.origin: An informal awareness observance promoted by self-help and wellness communities as a reminder that attitude can shape your day. It has no single official founder.
holidays.funFact: Researchers who study optimism have found links between positive outlooks and better coping with stress, but they also note that forced positivity can backfire.

holidays.name: Roald Dahl-ish Day: Star-Spangled Banner Day
holidays.description: A patriotic observance marking the day Francis Scott Key finished writing the poem that became the U.S. national anthem, inspired by a battle he watched from a ship.
holidays.origin: On September 14, 1814, after the bombardment of Fort McHenry in Baltimore during the War of 1812, Key saw the American flag still flying and wrote the poem 'Defence of Fort M'Henry.' It was later set to a popular British tune and became 'The Star-Spangled Banner.'
holidays.funFact: The tune came from 'To Anacreon in Heaven,' a drinking song for a London gentlemen's club, and the anthem wasn't made official until 1931.
